gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-warang-ci: Commanding and a little ominous, Bloody drops big round lowercase bowls onto the page, while Noto Sans Warang Citi sets its words as solid blocks. Wide channels lead into every counter.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-yi: Bloody hits hard with big round lowercase bowls and a commanding, bloody swagger. And Noto Sans Yi, a plain sans, does the quieter job, with a deep midsection and rounds left unsealed like an unlatched hook.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-zanabazar: Heavy, dripping drama up top. Underneath, Noto Sans Zanabazar Square keeps wide gaps and a soaring x-height, so paragraphs of text stay crisp and friendly even at tiny sizes beside Bloody.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-traditional-nu: Noto Traditional Nushu reads like a broad-nibbed pen stroke that never curls shut, with bowls filling the line. And Bloody, with its big round lowercase bowls, gives that approachable body a commanding, bloody headline.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-numans: Big round lowercase bowls give Bloody its commanding, bloody look, and nothing about it whispers. Numans follows with an s whose ends hang far from the spine and tracking pushed well past normal, so text feels stretched and modern.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-onest: Fat, round and menacing, Bloody swells where its curves meet the stems. And Onest stays gentle, with short ascenders above big bowls, so you can size it up or down without losing that smooth line.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-open-sans: Big, round and bloody, the heading shouts first. But Bloody is built for impact, while Open Sans is built for a smooth read, with bulky lowercase proportions and no clogged curves.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-orienta: Bloody is all commanding presence, with big round lowercase bowls. Orienta sits beneath it with counters that breathe like a hollow reed cut open and little height difference between cases, giving the loud heading some room to land.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-oxygen: Oxygen is the body here, a clean sans-serif whose curves never close back on themselves. Oxygen keeps lowercase nearly matching the capitals for easy text, while Bloody brings the big round, commanding, bloody drama.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-parkinsans: Bloody looks swollen and dangerous. Parkinsans is the opposite, a plain stripe of constant ink with wide-mouthed letters that stay crisp when shrunk, so the heading can roar while the text just gets on with it.
